jp-20260916-news-3.title: OpenAI Skeptical About 2026 IPO, Likely Prioritizing AI Agent Safety

segments.src: ## 年内上場を巡る発言が波紋
segments.tr: ## Remarks on IPO Timing Cause a Stir

segments.src: OpenAIのサム・アルトマンCEOが、2026年内の新規株式公開(IPO)について否定的な見解を示したと報じられている。これまで市場では、同社の企業価値の拡大や資金需要の高まりを背景に、年内または近い将来の上場観測が繰り返し取り沙汰されてきた。今回の発言は、そうした観測に一定のブレーキをかける内容として受け止められている。
segments.tr: It has been reported that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has expressed skepticism regarding an initial public offering (IPO) within 2026. Until now, market speculation has repeatedly suggested an IPO might happen within the year or in the near future, driven by the company's growing corporate value and increasing capital needs. These latest remarks are being interpreted as a move to put the brakes on such speculation.

segments.src: ## 背景にあるとされる「安全性優先」の姿勢
報道によれば、今回の方針転換の背景には、自律的にタスクを遂行する「AIエージェント」機能に関連する一連のトラブルへの対応があるとされる。AIエージェントは近年、単純な応答生成にとどまらず、外部サービスの操作やコード実行など、より広範な権限を伴う形で実用化が進んでいる分野であり、業界全体で安全性の確保が課題として指摘されてきた。
segments.tr: According to reports, this shift in policy is linked to addressing a series of issues related to "AI agent" functions, which autonomously execute tasks. In recent years, AI agents have moved beyond simple response generation into fields where they are being put to practical use with broader permissions, such as operating external services and executing code, and ensuring safety has been pointed out as a challenge for the entire industry.

segments.src: OpenAI側は、こうした状況を踏まえ、上場によって生じる短期的な業績・成長へのプレッシャーよりも、安全対策や検証プロセスの強化を優先する考えを示したとされている。ただし、具体的にどのような事案が判断材料となったのかについては、現時点で公式に詳細が明らかにされているわけではなく、続報が待たれる状況だ。
segments.tr: Given this situation, OpenAI is said to have indicated that it will prioritize strengthening safety measures and verification processes over the short-term pressure for performance and growth that comes with going public. However, no official details have been released at this time regarding exactly which incidents served as the basis for this decision, and further reports are awaited.

segments.src: ## アンソロピックの「開発減速論」にも改めて注目
segments.tr: ## Renewed Attention on Anthropic's "Development Slowdown" Argument

segments.src: 今回の一件を受けて、競合であるアンソロピック(Anthropic)がかねてより主張してきた、AI開発のペースを意図的に抑制すべきだとする、いわゆる「開発減速論」にも改めて関心が集まっている。アンソロピックは以前から、AIモデルの能力向上のスピードに対して、安全性検証や社会的な受け入れ態勢の整備が追いついていない可能性を指摘してきた経緯がある。
segments.tr: Following this news, renewed interest has gathered around the so-called "development slowdown" argument, which competitor Anthropic has long advocated, suggesting that the pace of AI development should be intentionally curbed. Anthropic has previously pointed out that safety verification and the development of social acceptance frameworks may not be keeping pace with the speed at which AI model capabilities are improving.

segments.src: 業界内では、OpenAIが仮に今回、安全性を理由に上場計画を先送りする判断をしたとすれば、これまで急速な実用化・商業化を推し進めてきた同社の姿勢にも変化の兆しがあるのではないか、との見方も出ている。もっとも、これはあくまで一部の観測にすぎず、両社の立場の違いが今後どのように収れんしていくかは不透明だ。
segments.tr: Within the industry, some are viewing this as a potential sign of change in OpenAI's stance, given that the company has previously pushed for rapid practical application and commercialization, if they have indeed decided to postpone IPO plans due to safety concerns. However, this is merely speculation, and it remains unclear how the differing positions of the two companies will converge in the future.

segments.src: IPOの時期そのものについては、企業側の資金調達戦略や株主構成、規制対応など複数の要因が絡むため、単一の要因だけで説明できるものではない。今回の報道が事実であれば、AIエージェントの安全性という技術的な課題が、企業の資本政策という経営判断にまで影響を及ぼした事例として注目される。
segments.tr: The timing of an IPO itself involves multiple factors, including the company's capital procurement strategy, shareholder composition, and regulatory compliance, and cannot be explained by a single factor alone. If these reports are true, it will be noted as a case where the technical challenge of AI agent safety has influenced management decisions regarding corporate capital policy.

segments.src: 生成AI・AIエージェント分野は各社が開発競争を続ける一方、誤動作や意図しない挙動への対応が引き続き重要なテーマとなっている。今後、OpenAIやアンソロピックを含む主要プレーヤーが、安全対策と事業成長のバランスをどのように取っていくのか、業界内外から注視が続きそうだ。
segments.tr: While companies continue to compete in the development of generative AI and AI agents, responding to malfunctions and unintended behaviors remains a critical theme. How major players, including OpenAI and Anthropic, will balance safety measures with business growth will continue to be closely watched both inside and outside the industry.

segments.src: ※本記事は現時点で報じられている内容に基づくものであり、詳細については各社の公式発表など今後の情報を確認する必要がある。
segments.tr: ※ This article is based on information reported as of this moment; please check future information, such as official announcements from the companies, for details.

jp-20260916-news-1.title: Chubu Electric Power withdraws application for safety review of Hamaoka Nuclear Power Plant Units 3 and 4; President Hayashi and Chairman Katsuno resign to take responsibility

segments.src: 中部電力は、静岡県御前崎市にある浜岡原子力発電所3号機・4号機の再稼働に向けて原子力規制委員会に提出していた安全審査の申請を取り下げると発表しました。あわせて、林欣吾社長と勝野哲会長が引責辞任する人事も明らかにされています。
segments.tr: Chubu Electric Power has announced that it will withdraw its application for safety reviews submitted to the Nuclear Regulation Authority for the restart of Units 3 and 4 of the Hamaoka Nuclear Power Plant located in Omaezaki City, Shizuoka Prefecture. Alongside this, management changes have been revealed in which President Kingo Hayashi and Chairman Tetsu Katsuno will resign to take responsibility.

segments.src: ## 何が問題になったのか

今回の対応の背景にあるのは、再稼働審査に必要な地震想定に関するデータの取り扱いをめぐる問題です。同社の社内調査により、審査資料に用いられたデータの一部について、適切とは言えない処理が行われていたことが判明したとされています。中部電力はこの事実を重く受け止め、審査の前提となる資料の信頼性を確保できない状態のまま手続きを続けることは適切ではないと判断し、規制委員会への申請を自主的に取り下げる方針を固めたということです。
segments.tr: Behind this decision is an issue concerning the handling of data related to earthquake assumptions necessary for the restart review. According to an internal investigation by the company, it was found that inappropriate processing had been performed on some of the data used in the review materials. Chubu Electric Power has taken this fact seriously, determining that it is inappropriate to continue procedures while unable to ensure the reliability of the materials serving as the premise for the review, and has solidified its policy to voluntarily withdraw the application to the Regulation Authority.

segments.src: ## 経営責任と今後の体制

中部電力は、今回の問題を経営として重く受け止めるとして、林社長と勝野会長がそれぞれの役職を退く意向を表明しました。両氏の辞任は、審査資料の管理体制や社内のチェック機能が十分に機能していなかったことへのけじめとして位置づけられています。会社側は今後、後任の経営体制のもとで、データ管理や品質保証に関する社内プロセスの見直しを進める方針を示しており、再発防止に向けた具体策についても順次公表するとみられます。
segments.tr: Taking the current issue seriously as management, Chubu Electric Power announced the intention of President Hayashi and Chairman Katsuno to step down from their respective positions. The resignation of both individuals is positioned as a settlement for the fact that the review material management system and internal check functions were not functioning sufficiently. The company has indicated a policy to review internal processes related to data management and quality assurance under a successor management structure moving forward, and concrete measures for recurrence prevention are expected to be announced sequentially.

segments.src: ## 浜岡原発を取り巻く状況
segments.tr: ## Situation Surrounding Hamaoka Nuclear Power Plant

segments.src: 浜岡原発は、想定される大規模地震の震源域に近い立地であることから、これまでも耐震性や津波対策をめぐって高い関心が寄せられてきた発電所です。3号機・4号機は東日本大震災後の停止以来、長期にわたり運転を停止した状態が続いており、再稼働には規制委員会による審査への合格が前提となります。今回の申請取り下げにより、両号機の再稼働時期はあらためて不透明な状況となりました。
segments.tr: The Hamaoka Nuclear Power Plant is a facility that has historically garnered high interest regarding seismic resistance and tsunami countermeasures due to its location close to the hypocentral region of anticipated large-scale earthquakes. Units 3 and 4 have remained shut down for a long period since the Great East Japan Earthquake, and passing the review by the Regulation Authority is a prerequisite for restarting. With this withdrawal of the application, the timing for the restart of both units has once again become unclear.

segments.src: 中部電力は、データの取り扱いに関する経緯の検証を継続するとともに、地元自治体や住民への説明を丁寧に行っていく考えを示しています。今後は、原因究明の結果や再発防止策の内容、そして審査再申請の是非やスケジュールに関する会社側の説明に注目が集まりそうです。同社の対応や規制委員会とのやり取りの推移について、引き続き情報が更新される見通しです。
segments.tr: Chubu Electric Power has indicated its intention to continue verifying the circumstances surrounding the data handling while carefully explaining the situation to local governments and residents. Moving forward, attention is likely to focus on the results of the investigation into the causes, the contents of recurrence prevention measures, and the company's explanations regarding the pros and cons and schedule of reapplying for the review. Information is expected to continue to be updated regarding the company's response and the progression of interactions with the Regulation Authority.

jp-20260916-news-2.title: Tohoku Corporate Business Sentiment Improves for the First Time in 3 Quarters: Automotive-Related Manufacturing Underpins Regional Economy

segments.src: ## 東北地区の景況感、3期ぶりにプラスへ
segments.tr: ## Business Sentiment in the Tohoku Region Turns Positive for the First Time in 3 Quarters

segments.src: 日銀短観をはじめとする各種企業アンケート調査によると、東北地区の企業景況感を示す指数が、3四半期ぶりに改善の方向へ転じたとみられる。これまで足踏みが続いていた地域経済に、明るい兆しが見え始めている格好だ。
segments.tr: According to various corporate survey data, including the Bank of Japan's Tankan, the index indicating corporate business sentiment in the Tohoku Region is seen to have shifted toward improvement for the first time in three quarters. Bright signs are beginning to emerge in the regional economy, which had previously experienced a standstill.

segments.src: ## 自動車関連を中心とした製造業が牽引役に
segments.tr: ## Manufacturing Centered on Automotive-Related Industries Acts as the Driving Force

segments.src: 今回の改善を主導しているのは、自動車関連を中心とした製造業とされる。東北地区は完成車メーカーの生産拠点や、部品・素材を供給するサプライヤーが数多く集積する地域であり、自動車産業の稼働状況が地域経済全体の体感に直結しやすい構造を持つ。
segments.tr: This improvement is reportedly being led by manufacturing centered on automotive-related industries. The Tohoku Region is an area where numerous production bases of finished car manufacturers and suppliers providing parts and materials are concentrated, possessing a structure where the operational status of the automotive industry is directly linked to the overall perceived condition of the regional economy.

segments.src: 半導体をはじめとする部材の供給環境が徐々に落ち着きを取り戻し、生産計画を立てやすくなったことが、現場の景況感を押し上げた一因として挙げられている。また、電動化や省人化に向けた設備投資の動きも、関連する製造業や周辺のサービス業にとって追い風になっているとの見方がある。
segments.tr: The recovery of stability in the supply environment for components such as semiconductors, making it easier to formulate production plans, is cited as a factor that pushed up business sentiment on the ground. Additionally, there is a view that equipment investment movements toward electrification and labor-saving are acting as a tailwind for related manufacturing and surrounding service industries.

segments.src: ## 一方で非製造業には慎重な声も
segments.tr: ## On the Other Hand, Cautious Voices Exist Among Non-Manufacturing

segments.src: 製造業の底堅さが目立つ一方、非製造業や中小企業の間では、原材料やエネルギーコストの上昇、人手不足による採用難など、依然として慎重な見方も根強いとされる。改善の実感が業種や企業規模によって濃淡があることには、注意が必要だろう。
segments.tr: While the resilience of manufacturing stands out, cautious views remain deeply rooted among non-manufacturing and small to medium-sized enterprises due to factors such as rising raw material and energy costs, and recruitment difficulties caused by labor shortages. Attention must be paid to the fact that the sense of improvement varies in intensity depending on the industry type and company scale.

segments.src: ## 先行きを左右する要因
今後の焦点は、この改善傾向がどこまで持続するかにある。
segments.tr: The future focus lies on how long this improvement trend will be sustained.

segments.src: - 為替相場の動向が輸出関連企業の採算にどう影響するか
segments.tr: - How foreign exchange rate trends will impact the profitability of export-related companies

segments.src: - 世界的な自動車需要、とりわけ電動車シフトのペースがどう推移するか
segments.tr: - How global automotive demand, especially the pace of the electric vehicle shift, will progress

segments.src: - 原材料価格や人件費の上昇が企業収益をどの程度圧迫するか
segments.tr: - To what extent rising raw material prices and labor costs will pressure corporate earnings

segments.src: - 人手不足への対応として省力化投資がどこまで広がるか
segments.tr: - How far labor-saving investments will spread as a response to labor shortages

segments.src: こうした要因が絡み合う中で、東北地区の企業がどのように次の一手を打っていくのかが注目される。
segments.tr: Amid the intertwining of these factors, attention will be focused on how companies in the Tohoku Region will make their next moves.

segments.src: 3四半期ぶりの景況感改善は、自動車関連製造業の底堅さに支えられた側面が大きく、地域経済にとって前向きな材料といえる。ただし業種間のばらつきやコスト増といった課題も残っており、今後の統計や企業動向を注視していく必要がありそうだ。
segments.tr: The improvement in business sentiment for the first time in three quarters is largely supported by the resilience of automotive-related manufacturing, which can be said to be a positive material for the regional economy. However, challenges such as disparities among industries and increased costs remain, and it seems necessary to closely monitor future statistics and corporate trends.

jp-20260916-intro-marketing-13.title: [Marketing #13] That New Customer, If It Ends in One Purchase, It's a Loss—CRM and Performance Marketing Measured by LTV

segments.src: > 顧客は「1回いくら買ったか」ではなく「生涯でいくら利益を残すか」で見る。その数字がLTVで、それを育てる仕組みがCRM、投資効率を測るのがパフォーマンスマーケティングです。
segments.tr: > Customers should be evaluated not by "how much they bought in a single purchase," but by "how much profit they leave over their lifetime." That figure is LTV, the mechanism to nurture it is CRM, and the tool to measure investment efficiency is performance marketing.

segments.src: 広告を出して新規客が100人来た。売上も伸びた。——これは成功でしょうか。判断できません。その100人が二度と来なければ、広告費のほうが高くつくかもしれないからです。
segments.tr: You ran ads and got 100 new customers. Sales also grew. Is this a success? You can't tell. Because if those 100 people never come back, the ad spend might end up being higher.

segments.src: そこで使うのが**LTV（顧客生涯価値）**。1人の顧客が取引を続ける間に、企業へどれだけの利益を残すかを表す数字です。ざっくり書くとこうなります。
segments.tr: That's where **LTV (Customer Lifetime Value)** comes in. It's a figure representing how much profit a single customer leaves for the company while continuing transactions. Roughly written, it looks like this.

segments.src: LTV = 平均購入単価 × 粗利率 × 購入頻度 × 継続期間
segments.tr: LTV = 平均購入単価 × 粗利率 × 購入頻度 × 継続期間

segments.src: 対になるのが**CAC（顧客獲得コスト）**。広告費や販促費を、それで獲得できた新規客数で割った「1人連れてくるのにかかった費用」です。判断はシンプルで、`LTV > CAC` でなければビジネスは続きません。SaaSなどでは「LTVはCACの3倍を目安に」とよく言われますが、これは業界慣習の目安であって法則ではありません。在庫を持つ小売と月額課金では適正値が違います。
segments.tr: Paired with it is **CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost)**. It's the "cost it took to bring in one person," calculated by dividing ad and promotion expenses by the number of new customers acquired through them. The judgment is simple: if `LTV > CAC`, the business cannot continue. In SaaS and other industries, it is often said that "LTV should be around 3 times CAC," but this is an industry custom guideline, not a law. The appropriate value differs between physical retail and monthly subscriptions.

segments.src: LTVを上げる打ち手がCRM（顧客関係管理）です。CRMは「高いシステムを買うこと」ではなく、**誰がいつ何を買ったかを記録し、その人に合った接点を設計する考え方**のこと。定番の道具が**RFM分析**——直近購入日（Recency）、頻度（Frequency）、金額（Monetary）の3軸で顧客を分けます。「先月10万円買った常連」と「2年前に一度だけ買った人」に同じメールを送らない、というだけで成果は変わります。
segments.tr: The initiative to raise LTV is **CRM (Customer Relationship Management)**. CRM is not about "buying an expensive system," but rather **the mindset of recording who bought what and when, and designing touchpoints suited to that person**. A classic tool is **RFM Analysis**—segmenting customers along three axes: Recency, Frequency, and Monetary value. The results change just by avoiding sending the same email to "a regular who spent 100,000 yen last month" and "someone who bought just once two years ago."

segments.src: そして、その施策の費用対効果を数字で回すのが**パフォーマンスマーケティング**。CPA（1件獲得あたり費用）やROAS（広告費に対する売上倍率）を見ながら、クリエイティブや配信先を差し替えていきます。
segments.tr: And running the cost-effectiveness of those measures with numbers is **performance marketing**. While looking at CPA (Cost Per Acquisition) and ROAS (Return On Ad Spend), you swap out creatives and delivery destinations.

segments.src: ただし注意点が2つ。第一に、**測れる施策に予算が偏りがち**なこと。検索広告の数字は美しく出ますが、そもそもブランドを知らなければ誰も検索しません。第二に、**相関は因果ではない**こと。クーポンを送った人の来店率が高くても、それは「もともと来る気だった人がクーポンを開いた」だけかもしれません。判定するには、あえて送らない対照グループと比べる必要があります。
segments.tr: However, there are two points to note. First, **budgets tend to lean toward measurable measures**. Search ad numbers look great, but if people don't know the brand in the first place, no one searches. Second, **correlation is not causation**. Even if the store visit rate of people who received a coupon is high, it might just be that "people who were going to come anyway opened the coupon." To determine this, you need to compare with a control group to whom you dare not send it.

segments.src: 東京・中野の個人経営の美容室を想像してください。
segments.tr: Imagine a privately run hair salon in Nakano, Tokyo.

segments.src: 客単価7,000円、粗利率50%、来店は年4回、平均3年通う。すると `7,000 × 0.5 × 4 × 3 = 42,000円` がLTVです。一方、クーポンサイト経由の新規客1人にかかるコストが8,000円なら、LTVはCACの約5倍。十分に見合います。
segments.tr: Average customer spend of 7,000 yen, gross profit margin of 50%, visits 4 times a year, averaging 3 years of patronage. Then `7,000 × 0.5 × 4 × 3 = 42,000 yen` is the LTV. On the other hand, if the cost to acquire one new customer via a coupon site is 8,000 yen, LTV is about 5 times CAC. It is well worth it.

segments.src: ところが実際に集計すると、クーポン経由の新規客の6割が**1回で来なくなっていた**。その層のLTVは `7,000 × 0.5 × 1 = 3,500円`。CAC 8,000円を下回り、来てもらうほど赤字です。売上だけ見ていると絶対に気づけません。
segments.tr: However, when actually tallied, 60% of new customers via coupon sites **stopped coming after one visit**. The LTV of that segment is `7,000 × 0.5 × 1 = 3,500 yen`. It falls below the 8,000 yen CAC, and the more they visit, the more it operates at a loss. If you only look at sales, you would never notice.

segments.src: ここでCRMの出番です。予約台帳とLINE公式アカウントを紐づけ、「前回来店から90日経った人」を毎週リスト化して、担当スタイリスト名を入れた一言を送る。RFM分析のうち、まずR（直近来店日）だけを使う最小構成です。結果、来店頻度が年4回から年5回になれば `7,000 × 0.5 × 5 × 3 = 52,500円`。1人あたり1万円以上のLTV改善で、これは広告費ゼロで生まれた差です。
segments.tr: This is where CRM comes in. Linking the reservation ledger and the LINE official account, listing "people for whom 90 days have passed since their last visit" every week, and sending a short message including the assigned stylist's name. It is a minimal configuration that uses only R (Recency) out of RFM analysis. As a result, if the visit frequency increases from 4 times a year to 5 times, `7,000 × 0.5 × 5 × 3 = 52,500 yen`. An LTV improvement of over 10,000 yen per person, which is a difference generated with zero ad spend.

segments.src: さらにパフォーマンスマーケティング的に詰めるなら、Instagram広告のクリエイティブを2種類配信してCPAを比べ、8,000円を6,000円に下げる。同時に、送信対象の1割にはあえてメッセージを送らず、来店率を比較して「メッセージが本当に効いたのか」を確かめる——ここまでやって初めて、数字を根拠に予算を動かせます。
segments.tr: Furthermore, if you want to tighten it in a performance marketing way, you deliver two types of Instagram ad creatives to compare CPA, lowering 8,000 yen to 6,000 yen. At the same time, you dare not send a message to 10% of the target audience, compare visit rates, and verify whether "the message really worked"—only by doing this much can you move your budget based on numbers.

segments.src: 1. 顧客は売上ではなくLTV（生涯で残す利益）で評価し、CAC（獲得コスト）と必ず並べて見る。
segments.tr: 1. Evaluate customers not by sales, but by LTV (profit left over a lifetime), and always view it alongside CAC (acquisition cost).

segments.src: 2. CRMはシステムの名前ではなく、顧客データをもとに接点を設計する考え方。RFMのような単純な切り口でも効果は出る。
segments.tr: 2. CRM is not the name of a system, but a mindset of designing touchpoints based on customer data. Effects can be produced even with simple angles like RFM.

segments.src: 3. パフォーマンスマーケティングはCPA・ROASで改善を回す手法だが、測れるものへの偏りと、相関を因果と誤読する罠に注意する。
segments.tr: 3. Performance marketing is a method to drive improvements using CPA and ROAS, but beware of the bias toward what is measurable and the trap of misreading correlation as causation.

segments.src: **Q1.** 平均購入単価5,000円、粗利率50%、購入頻度が年3回、平均継続期間2年の顧客のLTVは？
segments.tr: **Q1.** What is the LTV of a customer with an average purchase unit price of 5,000 yen, a gross profit margin of 50%, a purchase frequency of 3 times a year, and an average retention period of 2 years?

segments.src: **Q2.**（O/X）CRMとは、高機能な顧客管理システムを導入すること自体を指す。
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) CRM refers to the act of introducing a high-function customer management system itself.

segments.src: **Q3.** 「クーポンを送った顧客の来店率が高かったので、クーポンに効果があった」と結論づける前に必要なものは？
segments.tr: **Q3.** What is necessary before concluding that "coupons were effective because the visit rate of customers who received coupons was high"?

segments.src: - **LTV（顧客生涯価値）**：1人の顧客が取引期間全体でもたらす利益の総額。
segments.tr: - **LTV (Customer Lifetime Value)**: The total profit brought by a single customer over the entire transaction period.

segments.src: - **CAC（顧客獲得コスト）**：新規顧客を1人獲得するのにかかった費用。広告・販促費 ÷ 獲得人数。
segments.tr: - **CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost)**: The cost required to acquire one new customer. Ad and promotion expenses ÷ Number of customers acquired.

segments.src: - **CRM（顧客関係管理）**：顧客データを蓄積・活用し、既存顧客との関係を維持・深化させる考え方と、その仕組み。
segments.tr: - **CRM (Customer Relationship Management)**: The mindset and mechanism of accumulating and utilizing customer data to maintain and deepen relationships with existing customers.

segments.src: - **RFM分析**：直近購入日・購入頻度・購入金額の3軸で顧客を分類する手法。
segments.tr: - **RFM Analysis**: A method of categorizing customers along three axes: recent purchase date, purchase frequency, and purchase amount.

segments.src: - **ROAS**：広告費に対して何倍の売上が得られたかを示す指標。利益ではなく売上ベースである点に注意。
segments.tr: - **ROAS**: An index showing how many times sales were obtained relative to ad spend. Note that it is based on sales, not profit.

segments.src: *正解: Q1 → B（5,000 × 0.5 × 3 × 2 = 15,000円。粗利率を掛け忘れると30,000円になります）／ Q2 → X（CRMは道具ではなく、顧客との関係を設計する考え方。台帳とLINEだけでも実践できます）／ Q3 → B（送った人の来店率が高いのは「もともと来る気だった人が反応した」可能性があり、送らないグループと比べて初めて効果を切り分けられます）*
segments.tr: *Correct Answer: Q1 → B (5,000 × 0.5 × 3 × 2 = 15,000 yen. Forgetting to multiply the gross profit margin makes it 30,000 yen) ／ Q2 → X (CRM is not a tool, but a mindset of designing relationships with customers. You can practice it with just a ledger and LINE) ／ Q3 → B (The high visit rate of those who received it may be because "people who were going to come anyway reacted," and effectiveness can only be isolated by comparing with a group that didn't receive it)*
